Ufufufufu......{p}

Oh, is that so.

Had I {f:upset|upset} her?

"{f:Sorry about that|I'm sorry}, Iwashita."{p}
rows.31:3fc0:
Iwashita glanced at {f:me|me}.
"You don't really dislike paintings, do you?"
..........What a pushy person {f:she was|she was}.
{f:I|I} sighed, and then nodded.
"No, I don't.
{f:I|I} love paintings, actually."
Hearing {f:my|my} answer, Iwashita seemed to cheer up again.{p}
rows.31:40d8:
What a wishy-washy person you are.
Can't you even decide cleanly whether you like something or not?{p}You're indecisive, aren't you?
rows.31:416c:
Then you can at least answer whether you like something or not, can't you?
Do you like paintings?
Or do you dislike them?{p}Make up your mind.
rows.31:41f0:
Hmm, so you dislike them.
Should you really say something like that?
After all, a painting holds the feelings of the person who painted it.
It's affected by their mood while painting, too, but which feeling do you think is the strongest?
......That's right: the wish to be seen by someone.
Artists all seem to have that urge to show themselves off, to some degree.
I suppose they have to, or they couldn't be artists.
But the feelings poured into a painting like that gradually become one with the painting.
And then the painting itself begins to wish that someone would look at it.
Have you ever heard stories about the eyes of a portrait moving to look at you?
Or people slipping out of paintings and walking around?
They do that because they want to stand out, too.
With that one single wish, 'Look at me,' they'll do even unbelievable things.
That's how strong the feeling is.{p}
rows.31:44c4:
And yet you say you dislike paintings.
Without even thinking about how the paintings who hear it will feel..........
How inconsiderate.
Paintings dislike tactless people like you, too.
......You'd better not think it doesn't matter if paintings hate you.
A painting with an especially strong will can live among us, looking no different from a human being.{p}
rows.31:4618:
Shall I tell you how I know such a thing?
Because I'm one of those paintings myself.
Well? I'm no different from an ordinary person, am I?
I was originally a portrait, but I switched places with the real Akemi Iwashita.
Where the real one went is... ufufu, a secret.{p}
rows.31:4700:
......What's wrong? You're making a funny face.
If you can't believe me, that's fine too.
But anyway, you dislike us paintings.
And I, on behalf of my kind, dislike you.
Be careful.
Making an enemy of me is a frightening thing......{p}
rows.31:47d4:
Just kidding.
It's a joke, a joke..........probably, ufufufu.
You were a little scared, weren't you?
So, who's telling the next story?{p}
rows.31:484c:
I thought so.
In that case, just decide that you like paintings.{p}All right? That's fine, isn't it?
rows.31:49e4:
Oh, is that so.
After I've gone this far for you.
I don't want to talk to you anymore.
rows.31:4acc:
I see. What a shame.
But painting does take a special talent, doesn't it?
It's no use telling someone without it to paint.
Even if they managed it, it would be a dead painting.{p}
rows.31:4ba8:
......Oh, well.
I thought it would be quicker if you could see it for yourself.
The truth is, before I came here, I stopped by the art room.
And I picked out one portrait from among all the paintings and hung it up.
Why, you ask?
......Because the story I'm about to tell is about that painting.{p}
rows.31:4e00:
They say it was just before the painting was finished.
To this day, no one knows who killed her.
The killer was never caught.
rows.31:4e64:
It seems someone strangled her to death on her way home from school.
It might have been a random attacker.
Or maybe it was planned......
Shimizu must have been so bitter.
Back then she always stayed late in the art room, painting, so she could enter that picture in the prefectural competition.
......And then, just before the painting was finished, tragedy struck.{p}
rows.31:4fac:
Say, {a}{f:|}.
Can you imagine what became of that unfinished painting?
The one I hung in the art room, I mean.
The truth is, it was finished.
Strange, isn't it? Shimizu was supposed to have been killed before she finished it.
I'll tell you how such a thing could happen.{p}
rows.31:50cc:
Oh, are you really sure?
An eerie presence is starting to fill this room, too.
We've already told two of the seven wonders, after all.
You mean to stay here alone, in a place like this?
......Well, if that's what you want, I don't mind.
But you're a strange one.
I'd never do it, not for anything.
Well then, we're going, but if you change your mind, come after us.{p}
rows.31:521c:
Everyone except {f:me|me} stood up and began filing out of the room.
Iwashita, the last to go, looked back at {f:me|me}.{p}
rows.31:52c4:
"Be careful......"
She giggled softly.
A chill ran down my spine.
Did she know something?
Suddenly the thought of being left alone in this room frightened me.
"W... Wait!"
I hurriedly stood up.
"I'll come after all."
"I see......"
Iwashita, who had been about to close the door, gave me a broad smile.
"A wise choice."{p}
rows.31:53f4:
You don't feel it?
You really don't feel anything?
Was I mistaken when I thought you had a sixth sense?
Well, never mind.
Let's go on with the story.{p}
rows.31:5480: Don't say such a thing.{p}Let's hang it up for her, all right?
rows.31:54bc: It's fine to hang it up
rows.31:54f4:
How cold you are.
Then surely it's all right if I at least lean it against this easel.
rows.31:5548:
......There, that will do.
Shall we go back to the club room?
rows.31:55ec:
On the wall in front of us.
That painting is hanging there!
Did one of you just hang that painting on the wall?

rows.31:56e0:
......Oh, {a}{f:|}, you look pale.
Could it be... you're scared?
How hopeless. {f:And you call yourself a boy|You can't be like that}.
This is no more than the beginning.
The truly frightening part is still to come.
......Hm? You're asking if I know something?
Fufu, who can say?{p}
rows.31:5804:
You mustn't get angry.
Look, that painting is watching.
You mustn't get angry in front of a painting that harbors such a strong grudge.
That grudge has only just settled down, and it might awaken.{p}
rows.31:58bc:
That painting...... don't you feel as if it's glaring at you?
..........What's wrong?
You've gone white as a sheet.
Did you see something, maybe?
Like the painting's face changing..........
Not that I know anything. I'm only making it up.
Come on, let's go.{p}
rows.31:59b0:
......But, {a}{f:|}?
If you really did see something, you'd better be careful.
It might be sending a message to you.
If you don't notice it and ignore it......
Oh, I don't even want to think about that, do you?{p}
rows.31:5aac:
......Here we are.

In an instant, the painting went up in flames.
A pillar of fire roared up, several meters high.
And horribly, the flames swallowed up the teacher, who had been leaning over it.
The art club members rushed to put the fire out, but it was no use.
The teacher, a human fireball, was rolling around in agony, and they couldn't get near.{p}
rows.31:5dec: After a while the fire died down, but by then the teacher had already stopped moving.
rows.31:5e4c: Into that silence, as if the very air had frozen, someone's sudden scream broke.{p}
rows.31:5e98:
That person was pointing at the portrait.
......It must have caught fire, and yet there wasn't a single scorch mark on the portrait.
And that wasn't all.
Before it was set alight, it had certainly still been unfinished, but somehow the painting had been completed.
rows.31:5f7c: As if it had sucked the life out of the teacher.{p}
rows.31:605c:
But...... sometimes, they say, strange sounds can be heard coming from that painting.
A roaring whoosh, like something burning, and mixed in with it a voice, as if someone were crying, or laughing.
Is that the voice of the teacher who burned?

rows.31:6474:

rows.31:6598:
{f:I|I} screamed.

rows.31:672c:

Had {f:I|I} been so scared that I'd seen things, just as Iwashita said?{p}

The instant the flame touched the painting, it just went out, poof.
